title.zh: 卷一百二十一 周書12: 后妃列傳一
title.en: Volume 121 Book of Later Zhou 23: Biographies 1 - Empresses and Consorts
title.raw: 卷一百二十一 周書12: 后妃列傳一 Volume 121 Book of Later Zhou 23: Biographies 1 - Empresses and Consorts

sentences.zh: 太祖聖穆皇后柴氏，邢州龍崗人，世家豪右。

translations.literal: Empress Shenmu of Emperor Taizu, née Chai, was a native of Longgang in Xingzhou; her family were for generations eminent local magnates.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shenmu of Emperor Taizu, born into the Chai clan of Longgang in Xingzhou, came from a family that had long ranked among the region's great houses.

sentences.zh: 太祖微時，在洛陽聞後賢淑，遂聘之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was still obscure, in Luoyang he heard that the lady was virtuous and refined, and thereupon took her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: While he was still obscure, he heard in Luoyang of her virtue and refinement and took her as his wife.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·張永德傳》云：周太祖柴後，本唐莊宗之嬪御也。

translations.literal: (According to the 《Eastern Capital Miscellany·Biography of Zhang Yongde》: the Empress Chai of Emperor Taizu of Zhou had originally been a concubine of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Eastern Capital Miscellany》, Biography of Zhang Yongde, states that Empress Chai of Emperor Taizu of Zhou had originally been a concubine of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang.

sentences.zh: 莊宗沒，明宗遣歸其家，行至河上，父母迓之，會大風雨，止於逆旅數日。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong died, Mingzong sent her back to her family; on the road she reached the river, her parents came to meet her, and they were stopped by a great storm at an inn for several days.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong's death Mingzong sent her home; on the way to the Yellow River her parents came out to meet her, but a violent storm forced them to halt at an inn for several days.

sentences.zh: 有一丈夫走過其門，衣弊不能自庇。

translations.literal: A man ran past their door, his clothes in rags and unable to shelter himself.
translations.idiomatic: A man ran past the door in tattered clothes that could scarcely keep off the weather.

sentences.zh: 後見之，驚曰：「此何人邪？」

translations.literal: The lady saw him and said in astonishment, "Who is this man?"
translations.idiomatic: The lady saw him and cried out in surprise, "Who is this?"

sentences.zh: 逆旅主人曰：「此馬步軍使郭雀兒者也。」

translations.literal: The innkeeper said, "This is Guo Que'er, commissioner of the horse-and-foot army."
translations.idiomatic: The innkeeper answered, "That is Guo Que'er, commissioner of the horse-and-foot army."

sentences.zh: 後異其人，欲嫁之，請於父母。

translations.literal: The lady thought him extraordinary and wished to marry him; she asked her parents.
translations.idiomatic: Struck by his bearing, she wished to marry him and pleaded with her parents.

sentences.zh: 父母恚曰：「汝帝左右人，歸當嫁節度使，奈何欲嫁此人？」

translations.literal: Her parents said angrily, "You were a woman at the emperor's side; on returning home you ought to marry a military governor—why do you wish to marry this man?"
translations.idiomatic: Her parents were furious: "You had served at the emperor's side; now that you are home you should marry a military governor—why this man?"

sentences.zh: 後曰：「此貴人也，不可失也。

translations.literal: The lady said, "This man is of noble rank; he must not be let go.
translations.idiomatic: She replied, "This man is destined for greatness; we must not let him slip away.

sentences.zh: 囊中裝分半與父母，我取其半。」

translations.literal: She divided the contents of her purse in half for her parents and kept half for herself."
translations.idiomatic: She split her purse in two, gave half to her parents, and kept the rest."

sentences.zh: 父母知不可奪，遂成婚於逆旅中。

translations.literal: Her parents knew they could not prevail, and the marriage was completed at the inn.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing they could not dissuade her, her parents consented and the wedding was held at the inn.

sentences.zh: 所謂郭雀兒，即周太祖也。）〉

translations.literal: The so-called Guo Que'er was none other than Emperor Taizu of Zhou.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Guo Que'er in question was none other than the future Emperor Taizu of Zhou.)〉

sentences.zh: 太祖壯年，喜飲博，好任俠，不拘細行，後規其太過，每有內助之力焉。

translations.literal: In his prime the Emperor loved drinking and gambling, delighted in chivalric adventure, and did not trouble over small proprieties; the lady admonished him when he went too far and often gave him strength within the household.
translations.idiomatic: In his prime he drank and gambled freely, loved bold adventure, and cared little for petty propriety; she checked his excesses and was a steady force within the household.

sentences.zh: 世宗皇帝即後之侄也，幼而謹願，後甚憐之，故太祖養之為己子。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong was her nephew; dutiful and prudent from youth, she pitied him deeply, so the Emperor raised him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong was her nephew; dutiful even as a boy, he won her deep affection, and the Emperor therefore raised him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗寢，後見五色小蛇入顴鼻間，心異之，知其必貴，敬奉愈厚，未及貴而厭代。

translations.literal: Once when the Emperor was asleep, the lady saw a small serpent of five colors enter between his cheek and nose; her heart marveled at it, knowing he would surely become exalted, and she served him with ever greater respect, yet before he attained eminence she died.
translations.idiomatic: Once while he slept she saw a small five-colored serpent slip between his cheek and nose; struck by the omen and sure he was destined for greatness, she honored him all the more—yet she died before he rose to power.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，乃下制曰：「義之深無先於作配，禮之重莫大於追崇。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne he issued an edict saying, "In depth of righteousness nothing comes before taking a spouse; in weight of ritual nothing is greater than posthumous elevation.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne he issued an edict: "In depth of righteousness nothing precedes the bond of marriage; in weight of ritual nothing surpasses posthumous honor.

sentences.zh: 朕當寧載思，撫存懷舊。

translations.literal: On the throne I constantly reflect and cherish what was and what is past.
translations.idiomatic: On the throne I dwell on her memory and cherish what we once shared.

sentences.zh: 河洲令德，猶傳荇菜之詩；

translations.literal: Her virtue by the rivers reached far; still the ode of the water shields is recited;
translations.idiomatic: Her virtue by the rivers still lives in the ode of the water shields;

sentences.zh: 媯汭大名，不及珩璜之貴。

translations.literal: Her great name at Gui and Rui did not yet attain the worth of her jade regalia.
translations.idiomatic: yet her great name at Gui and Rui never matched the honor her jade regalia deserved.

sentences.zh: 俾盛副笄之禮，以伸求劍之情。

translations.literal: Let the full rites of the secondary pin be performed to express the longing for the sword.
translations.idiomatic: Let the full rites of the secondary pin be performed to express my longing to keep faith with her.

sentences.zh: 故夫人柴氏，代籍貽芳，湘靈集慶。

translations.literal: Thus Lady Chai, her clan's fragrance handed down, gathered blessings like the Lady of the Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chai of old, her clan's fragrance handed down through generations, gathered blessings like the Lady of the Xiang.

sentences.zh: 體柔儀而陳闕翟，芬若椒蘭；

translations.literal: Gentle in bearing she displayed the falcon banner of office, fragrant as pepper and orchid;
translations.idiomatic: Gentle in bearing, she bore the regalia of rank, fragrant as pepper and orchid;

sentences.zh: 持貞操以選中珰，譽光圖史。

translations.literal: Holding steadfast conduct she was chosen within the palace gates, her fame shining in chronicles.
translations.idiomatic: steadfast in conduct, she was chosen within the palace, and her fame shines in the chronicles.

sentences.zh: 懿範尚留於閨閫，昌言有助於箴規。

translations.literal: Her fine model still remained in the inner quarters; her good words aided in admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Her fine example still lingers in the inner quarters; her wise words aided every admonition.

sentences.zh: 深惟望氣之艱，彌嘆藏舟之速，將開寶祚，俄謝璧臺。

translations.literal: Deeply she considered the hardship of reading fate's signs; the more she sighed at how swiftly the boat is hidden—when the precious succession was about to open, she suddenly left the jade terrace.
translations.idiomatic: She had long read the hardship of fate's signs and sighed at how swiftly life passes—just as the precious succession was about to open, she suddenly left the jade terrace.

sentences.zh: 宜正號於軒宮，俾潛耀於坤象，可追命為皇后。

translations.literal: She should receive her proper title in the lofty palace and let her hidden radiance shine in the earthly trigram; she may be posthumously invested as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Let her receive her proper title in the lofty palace and let her hidden radiance shine in the earthly realm; she is posthumously invested as Empress.

sentences.zh: 仍令所司定謚，備禮冊命。」

translations.literal: Let the relevant offices fix her posthumous title and complete the rites of investiture."
translations.idiomatic: Let the relevant offices fix her posthumous title and complete the rites of investiture."

sentences.zh: 既而有司上謚曰聖穆。

translations.literal: Thereupon the offices submitted the posthumous title Shenmu.
translations.idiomatic: The offices thereupon submitted the posthumous title Shenmu.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，太祖神主入廟，以後祔於其室。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, when Emperor Taizu's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple, the lady was enshrined with him in his chamber.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiande, when Emperor Taizu's spirit tablet entered the ancestral temple, she was enshrined beside him in his chamber.

sentences.zh: 淑妃楊氏，鎮州真定人。

translations.literal: Lady of Cultivated Virtue Yang, from Zhending in Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Cultivated Virtue Yang was a native of Zhending in Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 父洪裕，真定少尹。

translations.literal: Her father Hongyu was Vice Magistrate of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Hongyu served as Vice Magistrate of Zhending.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·楊廷璋傳》云：父宏裕，少漁貂裘陂，有以二石雁授之者，其翼一掩左，一掩右，曰：「吾北嶽使也。」

translations.literal: (According to the 《Eastern Capital Miscellany·Biography of Yang Tingzhang》: his father Hongyu in youth fished at Diaojiuqi Pond; someone gave him two stone geese, one wing covering left and one covering right, saying, "I am an envoy of the Northern Peak."
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Eastern Capital Miscellany》, Biography of Yang Tingzhang, relates that his father Hongyu fished as a youth at Diaojiuqi Pond when someone presented him with two stone geese, one wing covering the left and one the right, saying, "I am an envoy of the Northern Peak."

sentences.zh: 言訖不知所之。

translations.literal: When the words were finished he vanished, none knew where.
translations.idiomatic: With those words he vanished, and no one knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 是年生女，為周太祖淑妃，明年生廷璋。）〉

translations.literal: That year a daughter was born, who became Lady of Cultivated Virtue of Emperor Taizu of Zhou; the next year Tingzhang was born.)〉
translations.idiomatic: A daughter was born that year—the future Lady of Cultivated Virtue of Emperor Taizu of Zhou—and Tingzhang was born the year after.)〉

sentences.zh: 當河朔三鎮全盛之時，所屬封疆，制之於守帥，故韶顏美媛，皆被選於王宮。

translations.literal: When the three Hebei circuits were in full flower, their territories were controlled by the defending commanders, so fair-faced beauties were all selected for princely palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When the three Hebei circuits were at their height, each garrison commander controlled his own domain, and fair-faced beauties were routinely drafted into princely palaces.

sentences.zh: 妃幼以良家子中選，事趙王王镕。

translations.literal: The lady in youth was chosen as a girl of good family and served Prince of Zhao Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen in youth from a respectable family, she entered the service of Prince of Zhao Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 張文禮之亂，妃流離於外。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Zhang Wenli, the lady was cast adrift abroad.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhang Wenli's rebellion she was cast adrift in the chaos.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗在藩，錄其遺逸。

translations.literal: When Tang Mingzong was still in his princely domain, he recorded those left behind.
translations.idiomatic: While still a prince, Tang Mingzong gathered up those who had been left behind.

sentences.zh: 安重誨保庇妃家，致其仕進，父母即以妃嫁於鄉人石光輔，不數年嫠居。

translations.literal: An Chonghui sheltered her family and secured their advancement in office; her parents thereupon married the lady to a fellow townsman, Shi Guangfu, and within a few years she was widowed.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui protected her family and helped them advance in office; her parents then married her to a townsman named Shi Guangfu, and within a few years she was widowed.

sentences.zh: 太祖佐漢之初，屬聖穆皇后棄世，聞妃之賢，遂以禮聘之。

translations.literal: At the beginning when the Emperor aided Han, as Empress Shenmu had passed away, hearing of the lady's virtue he took her in marriage with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his service to the Later Han, after Empress Shenmu's death, he heard of the lady's virtue and took her as his wife with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 《宋史·楊廷璋傳》：有姊寡居京師，周祖微時欲聘之，姊不從。

translations.literal: 《History of Song·Biography of Yang Tingzhang》: He had an elder sister widowed in the capital; when the Zhou founder was still obscure he wished to marry her, and the sister would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The 《History of Song》, Biography of Yang Tingzhang, notes that he had an elder sister, a widow in the capital; when the Zhou founder was still obscure he sought to marry her, but she refused.

sentences.zh: 令媒氏傳言恐逼，姊以告廷璋。

translations.literal: He had the matchmaker convey words of threat and coercion; the sister told Tingzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the matchmaker back with words that sounded like threats; she told Tingzhang.

sentences.zh: 廷璋往見周祖，歸謂姊曰：「此人姿貌異常，不可拒。」

translations.literal: Tingzhang went to see the Zhou founder and on returning said to his sister, "This man's bearing is extraordinary; he must not be refused."
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhang went to see the Zhou founder and told his sister on returning, "This man's bearing is extraordinary; you must not refuse him."

sentences.zh: 姊乃從之。）

translations.literal: The sister then consented.)
translations.idiomatic: She then agreed.)

sentences.zh: 妃睦族撫孤，宜家內助，甚有力焉。

translations.literal: The lady harmonized her clan and nurtured orphans; within the household she was a great help.
translations.idiomatic: She kept her clan in harmony and cared for orphans, and was a strong support within the household.

sentences.zh: 晉天福末，卒於太原，因留葬於晉郊。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianfu of Jin she died in Taiyuan and was therefore left buried in the Jin suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jin Tianfu era she died in Taiyuan and was buried in the Jin suburbs.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年九月，追冊為淑妃。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Guangshun she was posthumously invested as Lady of Cultivated Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Guangshun 1 she was posthumously invested as Lady of Cultivated Virtue.

sentences.zh: 太祖凡一後三妃，及嵩陵就掩，皆議陪祔。

translations.literal: The Emperor had in all one empress and three consorts; when Songling was closed, all were discussed for joint enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had one empress and three consorts in all; when Songling was sealed, each was considered for joint enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 時以妃喪在賊境，未及遷窆，世宗乃詔有司於嵩陵之側，預營一冢以虛之，俟賊平即議襄事。

translations.literal: At the time, as the lady's remains lay in rebel territory and had not yet been moved for burial, Shizong ordered the offices to prepare a tomb beside Songling to stand empty, to discuss the funeral rites once the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Because her remains still lay in rebel-held territory and could not yet be moved, Shizong ordered the offices to prepare an empty tomb beside Songling, to be filled once the rebels were subdued.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年夏，世宗征河東，果成素誌焉。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Xiande, Shizong campaigned in Hedong and indeed fulfilled his long-held wish.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of Xiande 1 Shizong campaigned in Hedong and at last fulfilled his long-held wish.

sentences.zh: 貴妃張氏，恒州真定人也。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Zhang, a native of Zhending in Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Zhang was a native of Zhending in Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖記，成德軍節度判官、檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Ji was adjutant of the Chengde army and Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Ji served as adjutant of the Chengde army and Acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 父同芝，本州諮呈官、檢校工部尚書，事趙王王镕，歷職中要。

translations.literal: Her father Tongzhi was reporting officer of the prefecture and Acting Minister of Works; he served Prince of Zhao Wang Rong and held posts in the central administration.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Tongzhi was the prefecture's reporting officer and Acting Minister of Works; he served Prince of Zhao Wang Rong and rose to posts in the central administration.

sentences.zh: 天祐末，趙將張文禮殺王镕，以鎮州歸梁，莊宗命將符存審討平之。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianyou, the Zhao general Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong and surrendered Zhenzhou to Liang; Zhuangzong ordered the general Fu Cunshen to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianyou the Zhao general Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong and surrendered Zhenzhou to Liang; Zhuangzong sent Fu Cunshen to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 時妃年尚幼，有幽州偏將武從諫者，駐騑於家，見妃韶令，乃為其子聘之。

translations.literal: At the time the lady was still young; a partial commander from Youzhou, Wu Congjian, was quartered at her home, saw her fair and comely, and betrothed her to his son.
translations.idiomatic: She was still young when a subordinate commander from Youzhou named Wu Congjian was billeted at her home; struck by her grace, he betrothed her to his son.

sentences.zh: 武氏家在太原。

translations.literal: The Wu family lived in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu family lived in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖從漢祖鎮並門，屬楊夫人以疾終，無何武氏子卒，太祖素聞妃之賢，遂納為繼室。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed the Han founder in garrisoning Bingmen; as Lady Yang died of illness, before long the Wu son also died; the Emperor had long heard of the lady's virtue and took her as his successor consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor followed the Han founder to garrison Bingmen, Lady Yang died of illness; soon afterward the Wu son died as well. Having long heard of the lady's virtue, he took her as his successor consort.

sentences.zh: 太祖貴，累封至吳國夫人。

translations.literal: When the Emperor rose in rank, she was repeatedly ennobled up to Lady of the State of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: As he rose in rank she was repeatedly ennobled, eventually to Lady of the State of Wu.

sentences.zh: 漢隱帝末，蕭墻變起，屠害大臣，太祖在鄴都被讒，妃與諸皇屬同日遇害於東京舊第。

translations.literal: At the end of Han Yindi, trouble arose within the palace walls and ministers were slaughtered; the Emperor in Ye was slandered, and the lady with the imperial kin were killed on the same day at the old residence in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han Yindi's reign palace intrigue erupted and ministers were slaughtered; slandered while in Ye, the Emperor could not save her—she and the imperial kin were killed on the same day at his old residence in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，追冊為貴妃，發哀，故世宗有起復之命。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne he posthumously invested her as Honored Consort and proclaimed mourning; therefore Shizong had the order to resume office from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne he posthumously invested her as Honored Consort and proclaimed mourning, which is why Shizong later issued an order for him to leave mourning.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，以太祖舊宅即妃遇禍之地，因施為僧院，以皇建為名焉。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded, as the Emperor's old residence was where the lady met disaster, it was converted into a Buddhist monastery named Huangjian.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong succeeded, the Emperor's old residence—where she had met her end—was converted into a Buddhist monastery called Huangjian.

sentences.zh: 德妃董氏，常山靈壽人也。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Dong, a native of Lingshou in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort Dong was a native of Lingshou in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 祖文廣，唐深州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Wenguang was Recorder of Shenzhou in Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Wenguang had been Recorder of Shenzhou under Tang.

sentences.zh: 父光嗣，趙州昭慶尉。

translations.literal: Her father Guangsi was Commandant of Zhaoging in Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Guangsi served as Commandant of Zhaoging in Zhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 妃孩提穎悟，始能言聽，按絲管而能辨其聲。

translations.literal: As a child the lady was keen and bright; as soon as she could speak and listen, she could strike the strings and pipes and distinguish their sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child she was quick and bright; as soon as she could speak she could play string and wind instruments and tell each tone apart.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，遇鎮州亂，親黨羈離，與妃相失。

translations.literal: At age seven she met the turmoil in Zhenzhou; kin were scattered and she was lost from her family.
translations.idiomatic: At seven she was caught in the turmoil at Zhenzhou; her kin were scattered and she was separated from her family.

sentences.zh: 潞州牙將得之，匿於褚中。

translations.literal: A Lu prefecture guard officer obtained her and hid her in a sack.
translations.idiomatic: A guard officer from Lu prefecture seized her and hid her in a sack.

sentences.zh: 其妻以息女不育，得妃憐之，過於所生，姆教師箴，功容克備。

translations.literal: His wife, as her own daughter could not bear children, obtained the lady and cherished her more than a birth child; nurse and tutor instructed her, and her deportment was fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, who had no children of her own, took her in and loved her more than a daughter of her own blood; nurses and tutors trained her until her manners were flawless.

sentences.zh: 妃家悲念，其兄瑀諸處求訪，垂六七年。

translations.literal: The lady's family grieved and thought of her; her elder brother Yu sought her everywhere for nearly six or seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Her family mourned her loss; her elder brother Yu searched for her everywhere for nearly six or seven years.

sentences.zh: 後潞將入官於朝，妃之鄉親頗有知者，瑀見潞將，欣歸之，時年十三。

translations.literal: Later when the Lu commander entered office at court, several of the lady's townsfolk recognized her; Yu met the Lu commander and joyfully brought her home—she was then thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Lu commander came to court, townsfolk who knew her recognized her; Yu met the commander and brought her home in joy—she was thirteen.

sentences.zh: 妃歸逾年，嫁為里人劉進超之妻，進超為內職，及契丹破晉之歲，陷蕃歿焉，妃嫠居洛陽。

translations.literal: After more than a year at home the lady married Liu Jinchao, a fellow townsman; Jinchao held an inner-court post, and in the year the Khitans destroyed Jin he perished in captivity; the lady was widowed in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: A year after her return she married a townsman named Liu Jinchao, who held an inner-court post; when the Khitans overran Jin he died in captivity, and she was left a widow in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖楊淑妃與妃鄉親，平居恒言妃賢德。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu's Lady of Cultivated Virtue Yang was a fellow townsman of the lady and in daily life always spoke of her virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Cultivated Virtue Yang, a fellow townsman, often spoke in daily life of the lady's virtue.

sentences.zh: 太祖從漢祖幸洛，因憶淑妃之言，尋以禮納之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor followed the Han founder to Luoyang, recalling the Cultivated Virtue lady's words, he soon took her in marriage with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor accompanied the Han founder to Luoyang, he recalled Lady Yang's praise and soon took her as his wife with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 鼎命初建，張貴妃遇禍，中宮虛位，乃冊為德妃。

translations.literal: When the Mandate was first established, Honored Consort Zhang met disaster and the inner palace was vacant; she was then invested as Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was first founded, Honored Consort Zhang had been killed and the inner palace stood empty; she was invested as Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 太祖自聖穆皇后蚤世以來屢失邦媛，中幃內助惟妃存焉，加以結珮脫簪，率由令範。

translations.literal: Since Empress Shenmu's early death the Emperor had repeatedly lost consorts of the state; within the inner curtain she alone remained as household help, and moreover in tying sashes and removing hairpins she always followed the fine model.
translations.idiomatic: Since Empress Shenmu's early death he had lost consort after consort; she alone remained to manage the inner household, and in every detail of dress and deportment she set the standard.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年夏，遇疾，醫藥之際，屬太祖兗海之征，車駕將行，妃奏曰：「正當暑毒，勞陛下省巡，明發宵征，須人供侍，司簿已下典事者，各已處分從行。」

translations.literal: In summer of the third year of Guangshun she fell ill; while physicians attended her, it fell when the Emperor was campaigning in Yanhai and the imperial carriage was about to depart; the lady memorialized, "It is just the season of summer heat; Your Majesty labors in inspection tours, setting out at dawn and marching by night—attendants are needed; clerks and below in charge of affairs have each been assigned to accompany the journey."
translations.idiomatic: In summer of Guangshun 3 she fell ill. While physicians attended her, the Emperor was about to set out on the Yanhai campaign. She memorialized: "This is the season of summer heat, yet Your Majesty will tour the provinces, marching at dawn and through the night—you will need attendants. I have already assigned the clerks and other officers in charge to accompany you."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「妃疾未平，數令診視，此行在近，無繁內人。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The lady's illness is not yet settled; I have repeatedly ordered examinations—this journey is nearby; do not trouble the inner household."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your illness is not yet settled; I have ordered the physicians to watch you closely. This campaign is nearby—there is no need to trouble the inner household."

sentences.zh: 及太祖駐蹕魯中，妃誌欲令內人進侍，發中使往來言之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor halted in Lu, the lady resolved to have inner attendants come to serve and sent palace envoys back and forth to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: After he halted in Lu, she still wished to send inner attendants to wait on him and dispatched palace envoys to urge it.

sentences.zh: 太祖手敕鄭仁誨曰：「切慮德妃以朕至兗州行營，津置內人承侍。

translations.literal: The Emperor wrote by his own hand to Zheng Renhui: "I am deeply concerned that the Virtuous Consort, because I have reached the Yanzhou field headquarters, will arrange for inner attendants to come and serve.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wrote in his own hand to Zheng Renhui: "I am concerned that the Virtuous Consort, learning that I have reached the Yanzhou field headquarters, will arrange for inner attendants to come and serve me.

sentences.zh: 緣諸軍在野，不可自安，令鄭仁誨專心體候。

translations.literal: Because the armies are in the field, one cannot be at ease; order Zheng Renhui to attend to her with single-minded care.
translations.idiomatic: With the armies in the field I cannot be at ease about such arrangements. Let Zheng Renhui attend to her with your full attention.

sentences.zh: 如德妃津置內人東來，便須上聞約住，或取索鞍馬，不得供應。

translations.literal: If the Virtuous Consort arranges for inner attendants to come east, you must report upward and restrain them, or if they demand saddles and horses, do not supply them.
translations.idiomatic: If she arranges for inner attendants to come east, report at once and hold them back; if they demand saddles or horses, do not supply them.

sentences.zh: 如意堅確，即以手敕示之。」

translations.literal: If she is firm and resolute, show her this handwritten edict."
translations.idiomatic: If she insists, show her this handwritten edict."

sentences.zh: 既而平定兗州，車駕還京，妃疾無減，俄卒於大內，時年三十九。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yanzhou was pacified and the imperial carriage returned to the capital; the lady's illness did not lessen, and soon she died in the great inner palace—she was thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou was pacified and the Emperor returned to the capital, but her illness did not abate; she soon died in the inner palace at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 輟朝三日。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days.

sentences.zh: 妃長兄瑀，以左贊善大夫致仕，仲兄元之、季兄自明，皆累歷郡守。

translations.literal: The lady's eldest brother Yu retired as Left Supporter of the Heir Apparent; her second brother Yuanzhi and youngest brother Ziming had both repeatedly served as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Her eldest brother Yu had retired as Left Supporter of the Heir Apparent; her second brother Yuanzhi and youngest brother Ziming had each served repeatedly as prefect.

sentences.zh: 世宗貞惠皇后劉氏，將家女也，幼歸於世宗。

translations.literal: Empress Zhenhui of Emperor Shizong, née Liu, was a daughter of a military family and in youth became Shizong's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenhui of Emperor Shizong, née Liu, came from a military family and married Shizong in her youth.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，世宗在西班，後始封彭城縣君。

translations.literal: In Qianyou of Han, Shizong was in the western class; the lady was first ennobled as Lady of Pengcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: During the Han Qianyou era, while Shizong served in the western bureau, she was first ennobled as Lady of Pengcheng county.

sentences.zh: 世宗隨太祖在鄴，後留居邸第。

translations.literal: Shizong followed the Emperor in Ye; the lady remained in the residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong followed the Emperor to Ye, she remained at their residence.

sentences.zh: 漢末李業等作亂，後與貴妃張氏及諸皇族同日遇禍。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Li Ye and others made trouble; the lady with Honored Consort Zhang and the imperial kin met disaster on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han, when Li Ye and others rose in revolt, she, Honored Consort Zhang, and the imperial kin were killed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 國初，追封彭城郡夫人。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state she was posthumously ennobled as Lady of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty she was posthumously ennobled as Lady of Pengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年夏四月，追冊為皇后，謚曰貞惠，陵曰惠陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer of the fourth year of Xiande she was posthumously invested as Empress, posthumous title Zhenhui, tomb named Huiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer of Xiande 4 she was posthumously invested as Empress with the posthumous title Zhenhui; her tomb was named Huiling.

sentences.zh: 宣懿皇后符氏，祖存審，事後唐武皇、莊宗，位極將相，追封秦王。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanyi, née Fu; her grandfather Cunshen served Later Tang's Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong, rose to the summit of general and minister, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanyi, née Fu, was granddaughter of Cunshen, who served Later Tang's Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong, rose to the highest ranks of general and minister, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 父彥卿，天雄軍節度使，封魏王。

translations.literal: Her father Yanqing was military governor of the Tianxiong army and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yanqing was military governor of the Tianxiong army and held the title Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 後初適李守貞之子崇訓。

translations.literal: The lady was first married to Chongxun, son of Li Shouzhen.
translations.idiomatic: She was first married to Chongxun, son of Li Shouzhen.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，守貞叛於河中，太祖以兵攻之，及城陷，崇訓自刃其弟妹，次將及後，後時匿於屏處，以帷箔自蔽，崇訓倉黃求後不及，遂自刎，後因獲免。

translations.literal: In Qianyou of Han, Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong; the Emperor attacked with troops, and when the city fell Chongxun himself slew his younger siblings; next he was about to reach the lady, but she was then hiding behind a screen, covering herself with curtains; Chongxun in haste sought the lady but could not reach her and thereupon cut his own throat—the lady thereby escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: During the Han Qianyou era Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and the Emperor besieged him. When the city fell, Chongxun killed his younger siblings and was about to kill her next; she had hidden behind a screen, shielded by curtains. He searched for her in panic but could not find her in time and cut his own throat, and she escaped.

sentences.zh: 太祖入河中，令人訪而得之，即遣女使送於其父，自是後常感太祖大惠，拜太祖為養父。

translations.literal: When the Emperor entered Hezhong he had men seek and obtain her, and at once sent a female envoy to deliver her to her father; from then on the lady always felt the Emperor's great kindness and acknowledged him as adoptive father.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor entered Hezhong he had her found and at once sent a female envoy to return her to her father. From then on she was deeply grateful for his kindness and acknowledged him as her adoptive father.

sentences.zh: 世宗鎮澶淵日，太祖為世宗聘之。

translations.literal: On the day when Shizong was garrisoned at Chanyuan, the Emperor betrothed her to Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong was garrisoned at Chanyuan, the Emperor betrothed her to him.

sentences.zh: 後性和惠，善候世宗之旨，世宗或暴怒於下，後必從容救解，世宗甚重之，及即位，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: The lady's nature was gentle and kind; she was skilled at reading Shizong's intent; when Shizong sometimes raged at subordinates, the lady always calmly interceded and rescued them; Shizong greatly valued her, and when he took the throne she was invested as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and kind by nature, she read Shizong's moods well; when he flew into rages at his subordinates she would calmly intercede on their behalf. He valued her deeply, and when he took the throne he invested her as Empress.

sentences.zh: 世宗將南征，後常諫止之，言甚切直，世宗亦為之動容，洎車駕駐於淮甸，久冒炎暑，後因憂恚成疾。

translations.literal: When Shizong was about to campaign south, the lady often admonished and stopped him, her words very earnest and direct; Shizong was also moved by this; when the imperial carriage halted in the Huai region, long exposed to summer heat, the lady fell ill from worry and distress.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong prepared to campaign south she often urged him to stay, speaking with blunt earnestness that moved him; but when the imperial train halted in the Huai region, long exposure to summer heat and anxiety brought on her illness.

sentences.zh: 顯德二年七月二十一日，崩於滋德殿，時年二十有六。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month of the second year of Xiande she died in Zide Hall—she was twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month of Xiande 2 she died in Zide Hall at the age of twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 世宗甚悼之。

translations.literal: Shizong grieved for her deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong mourned her deeply.

sentences.zh: 既而有司上謚曰宣懿，葬於新鄭，陵曰懿陵。

translations.literal: Thereupon the offices submitted the posthumous title Xuanyi; she was buried at Xinzheng, tomb named Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: The offices thereupon submitted the posthumous title Xuanyi; she was buried at Xinzheng in the tomb named Yiling.

sentences.zh: （案：世宗有後符後，即宣懿之女弟也，薛史不為立傳，未免闕略。

translations.literal: (Note: Shizong had a later consort, the later Lady Fu, who was the younger sister of Xuanyi; Xue's History did not compose a separate biography for her, which is somewhat an omission.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: Shizong later had another consort, Lady Fu, the younger sister of Empress Xuanyi; Xue's History gives her no separate biography, which is a regrettable omission.

sentences.zh: 《五代史補》：世宗皇后符氏，即魏王彥卿之女。

translations.literal: 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Empress Fu of Shizong was the daughter of Prince of Wei Yanqing.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 states that Empress Fu of Shizong was the daughter of Prince of Wei Yanqing.

sentences.zh: 時有相工視之大驚，密告魏王曰：「此女貴不可言。」

translations.literal: At the time a physiognomist viewed her and was greatly startled, secretly telling the Prince of Wei, "This girl's nobility is beyond words."
translations.idiomatic: A physiognomist who examined her was greatly startled and told the Prince of Wei in secret, "This girl's destiny is beyond words."

sentences.zh: 李守貞素有異志，因與子崇訓娶之，禮畢，守貞甚有喜色。

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen had long harbored rebellious intent and therefore had his son Chongxun marry her; when the rites were complete Shouzhen showed great pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen, who had long harbored rebellious ambitions, had his son Chongxun marry her; when the wedding was complete he was visibly delighted.

sentences.zh: 其後據河中叛，高祖為樞密使，受命出征。

translations.literal: Afterward he held Hezhong and rebelled; the High Ancestor was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and received orders to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Later he seized Hezhong and rebelled; the High Ancestor, then Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was ordered to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 後知高祖與其父有舊，城破之際，據堂門而坐，叱諸軍曰：「我符魏王女也，魏王與樞密太尉，兄弟之不若，汝等慎勿無禮。」

translations.literal: The lady knew the High Ancestor and her father were old associates; as the city fell she sat by the hall door and shouted at the armies, "I am the daughter of Prince of Wei Fu; the Prince of Wei and the Grand Preceptor of the Bureau are as close as brothers—you must not be disrespectful."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the High Ancestor and her father were old associates, when the city fell she sat in the hall doorway and shouted at the soldiers, "I am the daughter of Prince of Wei Fu; the Prince of Wei and the Grand Preceptor are as close as brothers—you must not treat me with disrespect."

sentences.zh: 於是諸軍聳然引退。

translations.literal: Thereupon the armies drew back in awe.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers drew back in awe.

sentences.zh: 頃之，高祖至，喜曰：「此女於白刃紛之際保全，可謂非常人也。」

translations.literal: Before long the High Ancestor arrived and said with pleasure, "This girl preserved herself amid flashing blades—she may be called an extraordinary person."
translations.idiomatic: Soon the High Ancestor arrived and said with delight, "This woman preserved herself amid flashing blades—she is truly extraordinary."

sentences.zh: 乃歸之魏王。

translations.literal: He then returned her to the Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned her to the Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 至世宗即位，納為皇后。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne she was taken in as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne he made her his Empress.

sentences.zh: 既免河中之難，其母欲使出家，資其福壽，後不悅曰：「死生有命，誰能髡首跣足以求茍活也！」

translations.literal: After escaping the peril at Hezhong, her mother wished to have her leave home and become a nun to secure blessings and long life; the lady was displeased and said, "Life and death have their allotted span—who would shave the head and go barefoot to seek a mean survival!"
translations.idiomatic: After she escaped the disaster at Hezhong, her mother wished to have her take Buddhist orders to secure blessings and long life; the lady refused angrily: "Life and death are fated—who would shave her head and go barefoot merely to cling to life!"

sentences.zh: 母度不可逼，遂止。

translations.literal: Her mother judged she could not be compelled and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother saw she could not be forced and gave up the idea.

sentences.zh: 世宗素以後賢，又聞命不以出家為念，愈賢之，所以為天下母也。）〉

translations.literal: Shizong had always regarded the lady as virtuous, and hearing she would not consider leaving home for the tonsure, valued her all the more—thus she became mother of the realm.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had always known her for her virtue, and when he heard she would not take orders merely to prolong life, he esteemed her all the more—thus she became mother of the realm.)〉
